title: When to Use Microservices
description: Learn a decision framework for choosing microservices based on organizational readiness and technical constraints.

data.text: Microservices are not a default choice. They solve specific problems: scaling teams, independent deployment, and technology diversity. This lesson provides a decision framework to determine when microservices are the right choice.

terms.definition: The ability of the team and organization to operate microservices effectively.
The complexity of the business domain and its boundaries.
The need to deploy parts of the system independently.
The practice of building shared tooling and infrastructure for development teams.

items: Multiple teams blocked on shared deployments
Different parts of the system scale differently
The monolith is too large to understand

data.text: Microservices require network infrastructure, service discovery, distributed tracing, and centralized logging. If these are not in place, the operational burden can overwhelm the benefits.

data.caption: Microservices Decision Framework

data.title: Exercise: Readiness Assessment
data.description: Assess your current organization against the microservices readiness checklist.
steps: List your team size and structure
Recommend an architecture based on the score
data.expectedOutcome: A readiness assessment with scores and a justified recommendation

items.question: What is the #1 reason microservices fail?
items.answer: Adopting them without organizational readiness, especially platform engineering and operational maturity.

items.question: Can a small team use microservices?
items.answer: Rarely. Small teams usually benefit more from a modular monolith until they grow.

items.question: What is a modular monolith?
items.answer: A monolith with clear module boundaries, designed to be split into services later if needed.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: Use a decision framework, not hype
Organizational readiness matters more than technology
A modular monolith is often the right intermediate step
data.takeaway: Choose microservices when your team, domain, and scale justify the operational complexity.
